structured_output.what_is_happening: SPLIT (contract DRKGYsGALqr5p2aTcGLK9zqiPB5wk7JV78bJv4mPpump) is a pump.fun coin that migrated from its bonding curve to a PumpSwap AMM pool at 19:31:01Z, ~10 minutes before the detection rule fired at 19:41Z. In that ~10-minute post-migration window it did ~$460-480k of volume against a market cap running from the low tens of thousands up to $140-171k, with price up ~180-270% from the migration point (dexscreener/geckoterminal h1=h6=h24 figures are identical because the pool is only ~10 minutes old, so all "hourly" stats are really the same ~10-minute window). The project's own site, usesplit.pro (reached via GMGN's linked project_links, not found via search engine indexing), describes a Solana protocol that "splits token fees through X Money" with a $SPLIT token and buybacks, tied to X's (Twitter's) creator-monetization/payments push. GMGN links this exact contract to that website and the @Use_Split X handle, with no rename history for that account. However, the packet lists 9 other tokens sharing the exact name/ticker "SPLIT," most created within seconds to a couple minutes of each other (~1790451061000-1790451574000 ms), a classic sniper/bot-swarm clone pattern around a trending pump.fun graduation. This token is the earliest-created and highest-liquidity/mcap of that cluster, the strongest evidence it is the "winning" instance, but I could not independently confirm on X/search that community attention has coalesced around this specific contract rather than a sibling clone.

narrative.description: A Solana protocol claiming to split token/creator fees using X's (Twitter's) payments/monetization rails ("X Money"), with a $SPLIT token tied to buybacks. This taps a real, currently-live theme (X's rollout of payment/monetization features) but I found no independent evidence (news, X posts, Reddit) that this specific project or token is part of any actual discussion of that theme beyond its own marketing copy on usesplit.pro.
narrative.why_spreading: The observed volume spike ($460-480k in ~10 minutes) coincides exactly with the bonding-curve-to-AMM migration, which on pump.fun mechanically attracts sniper/bundler bots regardless of narrative quality. I found no organic external discussion (X, Reddit, news) driving this; the only narrative content is the project's self-description. A separate, unrelated legitimate project (SolSplits.xyz, a fee-splitting standard) explicitly states it has no token and that any token claiming affiliation is a scam, which adds naming confusion around the whole 'Split' concept space this token sits in.

token_connection.why_this_token: Among 10 tokens named/ticker'd SPLIT launched within minutes of each other, this contract is the earliest-created and has the highest liquidity ($37k) and market cap ($171k) of the cluster, and is the one GMGN's own metadata links to the usesplit.pro website and @Use_Split X account. That is the best available evidence it is the 'real' one, but search engines surfaced zero independent X/Reddit/news posts naming this contract or confirming which clone the community actually rallies behind.
token_connection.competing_tokens: 9 other SPLIT-named tokens found in the packet with mcaps from ~$3.7k to $184k and liquidity up to ~$30k, several created within 1-2 minutes of this one and one pair (58TPWfK...) with even higher mcap ($184k) than this token — genuine ambiguity about which is canonical.

authenticity.evidence: No X/Reddit/Telegram/news posts about this contract, ticker, or usesplit.pro were found via web search (search engines index X poorly and the site itself is not well indexed). GMGN wallet data shows 666 bundler wallets (44% of 1503 holders), 601 fresh wallets (40%), 37 sniper wallets, and a 52% bot/degen rate, with buys-per-unique-buyer of 1.96 — consistent with a bot/sniper swarm hitting a fresh migration rather than broad organic discovery.
authenticity.uncertainty: I cannot distinguish 'no organic attention exists' from 'organic attention exists on X but is invisible to my tools.' The high holder count (2883) and unique buyer count (2139 in ~10 min) is large in absolute terms even if bot-heavy, so some real money is clearly flowing, just of unclear composition.

structural_risks: Liquidity ($37k) is thin relative to the volume already transacted ($460k+), meaning slippage on any exit attempt by a bundler cluster could move price sharply.
666 bundler wallets and 37 sniper wallets represent a large latent sell-side overhang that could dump into any pump.
Price has already run +180-270% before this report's entry point, i.e., the trade is entering after most of the visible move, not before it.
9 near-identical clone tokens exist, so attention and liquidity could fragment or rotate to a sibling contract at any time.
Dev/creator's X account has launched 15 tokens historically with a prior best ATH mcap of only ~$204k, suggesting a ceiling pattern rather than a breakout pattern for this dev's launches.

structured_output.counterargument: My central worry is that the entry is happening after an already-completed, bot-driven pump (the 180-270% move happened in the 10 minutes before detection, mechanically tied to the bonding-curve migration, not to any narrative catalyst I can verify). A reasonable counter-view is that pump.fun migration volume of this size ($460k+ in minutes) genuinely does correlate with some subset of these coins continuing to run further as the migration liquidity unlock draws in momentum/copy-trading bots that chase already-pumping charts, and structurally this token is about as clean as they come (mint/freeze renounced, LP 100% locked, rugcheck score 1, zero dev holdings, no flagged risks) — so if any coin in this batch runs, clean structure plus already-proven liquidity absorption could make this one of the better-positioned candidates in the pool, even without a verified external narrative.

No Reddit, Telegram, Discord, or news-specific searches were attempted given budget.

structured_output.thesis: SPLIT is a freshly-migrated pump.fun graduate with clean on-chain structure (renounced authorities, 100% locked LP, zero dev holdings, no RugCheck flags) and a plausible-sounding but externally unverified narrative (X Money fee-splitting). The volume and price move that triggered detection occurred entirely within the ~10 minutes since AMM migration and is heavily populated by bundler/sniper/fresh wallets (bot/degen rate 52%), the signature of a migration-sniping swarm rather than confirmed organic demand. Nine near-identical same-name clones exist, adding real uncertainty about whether this is the contract attention will concentrate on. Because the entry happens after the visible pump already occurred, and because heavy bundler/sniper representation creates real overhang risk, I rate this below-average for hitting +100% before -50% in the next 30 minutes relative to a typical coin in this detection pool, while granting that clean structure and large absolute liquidity absorption keep it from being a bottom-tier candidate.
